answers.notes: Claim c39 of ch03 states directly that the power of a concave lens is negative (and convex is positive). No other option is supported.
answers.quote: You may note that the power of a convex lens is positive and that of a concave lens is negative.

answers.notes: The mismatched pair: thinking belongs to the forebrain (claim c27), while the medulla controls involuntary actions including blood pressure (claim c28), so 'medulla – blood pressure control' is correctly matched. Cerebellum–posture/balance is also correctly matched (claim c29).
answers.quote: The forebrain is the main thinking part of the brain.

answers.notes: Claim c34 ties Mendel to the laws of inheritance. The other pairs are contradicted by the claims: penicillin came from Fleming's mould (c29), blood circulation was Harvey's discovery (c33), and the smallpox vaccine was Jenner's (c31).
answers.quote: Mendel blended his knowledge of science and mathematics and was the first one to keep count of individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation. This helped him to arrive at the laws of inheritance.
